evidence.note: Explicitly stages a correctness-first PyTorch/cuBLAS baseline (step 3), then a dedicated correctness test (step 4), then a separate benchmark harness (step 5) — ordered milestones with distinct done-checks separating correctness from latency.

Keeps a frozen correct backup (kernel_fp32bak.py) and reverts each optimization (BF16, fused input projection) as soon as it fails correctness, treating performance as a separate track gated on a provably-correct baseline — prevents fast-but-wrong regressions.

Optimization stage decomposed per-component (Triton input LayerNorm, split/gating kernel, block-size tuning) with correctness re-checks and target-shape benchmarks per milestone; another frozen backup (kernel_lnopt_fp32.py) preserved and restored after a failed BF16-contraction experiment (step 23).

Before committing to a design change, benchmarks contraction alternatives (bench_contract.py) to localize the bottleneck rather than pushing monolithically — a targeted sub-goal within the optimization track.

reasoning: The agent runs clearly ordered milestones — correct baseline, correctness test, benchmark, then optimization — with each optimization gated on preserving a frozen correct backup that it reverts to on any correctness failure (steps 12-14, 22-23), and the optimization phase itself is decomposed per-component with per-milestone checks that prevent fast-but-wrong regressions (steps 21-25). This matches the level-8 description of ordered milestones with concrete exit tests and localized regressions, plus several level-10 traits (performance as a separate track on a frozen baseline, decomposed tuning). It falls short of 9-10 because the correctness exit-test was on small smoke cases rather than a demonstrated full shape/dtype/mask grid, and hardest-case (Cauchy/large-N) risk sequencing was not made explicit.
